problems.title: Vector between two side midpoints
problems.question: In parallelogram ABCD, T is the midpoint of BC and K of CD. AB=a and AD=b as vectors. Find TK.
problems.idea: Use A as the vector origin.

problems.title: Triangle area from a hypotenuse sum and difference
problems.question: In a right triangle, the hypotenuse minus one leg is 2m, and their sum is 2n. Find the area.
problems.idea: Solve for that leg and use a difference of squares for the other.
steps: Adding and subtracting gives c=m+n and a=n-m.
The other leg satisfies b²=(2m)(2n)=4mn, so b=2√(mn).
problems.note: The printed choice with 2(n-m)√(mn) is twice the correct area. Valid triangle data require n>m>0.

problems.title: Middle angle of a triangle in arithmetic progression
problems.question: A triangle’s angles form an arithmetic progression. Its middle-sized side is 15 cm. Find the area of its circumcircle.
problems.idea: The middle angle is one third of the angle sum.
formulas: A₁+A₂+A₃=180°; extended sine rule: side=2R sin(opposite angle).
steps: The middle angle is 60°, so the middle side 15 is opposite 60°.

problems.title: A quadratic for every parameter value
problems.question: Which listed equation remains quadratic for every real a?
problems.idea: Its x²-coefficient must never be zero.
formulas: A quadratic requires a nonzero leading coefficient.
steps: The coefficient a²+4a+9=(a+2)²+5 is strictly positive for every a.
Every other listed leading coefficient has real zeros.
Therefore (a²+4a+9)x²=0 is always quadratic, even though its root is always zero.

problems.title: A fourth-root factor cancels with a square-root difference
problems.question: Find the greatest value of $(\sqrt[4]x-2)/(\sqrt x-4)$.
problems.idea: Set t=⁴√x and preserve the excluded denominator value.
steps: The domain is x≥0,x≠16, so t≥0,t≠2.
Its maximum is 1/2 at t=0, corresponding to x=0.

problems.title: Area of an isosceles triangle inscribed in a circle
problems.question: An isosceles triangle is inscribed in a radius-6 circle and has altitude 8 cm to its base. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the circle to find the half-base.
steps: Put the apex at (0,6); the base is then at y=-2.
A base endpoint satisfies x²=36-4=32, so the half-base is 4√2.
The full base is 8√2 and the height is 8.

problems.title: Nested roots with a zero-parameter exception
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[3]{\frac{a^2}{x}\sqrt{\frac1x\sqrt{\frac a{x^3}}}}$.
problems.idea: State the original real domain before using fractional powers.
formulas: Even roots require nonnegative radicands; denominator x cannot be zero.
steps: If a=0 and x≠0, the expression is defined and equals zero.
If a≠0, the innermost root requires a,x to have the same sign; its positive value multiplied by 1/x requires x>0. Thus a>0,x>0.
On the positive case, the inner two roots combine to a^(1/4)x^(-5/4). Multiplying by a²/x and taking the cube root gives a^(3/4)x^(-3/4).
This is ⁴√(a³/x³), and that formula also equals zero in the allowed a=0 case.
problems.answer: $\sqrt[4]{a^3/x^3}$ on the domain: a=0,x≠0, or a>0,x>0.

problems.title: Common difference from two sequence terms
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₇=17 and a₁₇=19. Find its common difference.
problems.idea: The term indices are ten steps apart.

problems.title: Cancel a factor without restoring forbidden inputs
problems.question: Simplify $(a^2-ab-2b^2)/(a^2-3ab+2b^2)$.
problems.idea: Factor both quadratics.
steps: The original denominator requires a≠b and a≠2b.
The simplified form is (a+b)/(a-b), retaining both original exclusions.

problems.title: Fourth powers from quadratic root data
problems.question: If x₁,x₂ solve $x^2+\sqrt2x-\sqrt3=0$, find $x_1^4+x_2^4$.
problems.idea: Use the sum and product instead of individual roots.

problems.title: Factor using two square-root variables
problems.question: Simplify $[\sqrt{8x^2y}-2y\sqrt x-x\sqrt x]/(\sqrt{2y}-\sqrt x)$.
problems.idea: Let u=√x and v=√(2y).
steps: Cancel the nonzero denominator v-u to obtain -u(v-u)=u²-uv.

problems.title: A squared square root followed by an absolute value
problems.question: Simplify $(\sqrt{2-x})^2-\sqrt{x^2-6x+9}$.
problems.idea: Use the first radical’s domain when removing the second root.
steps: The domain is x≤2. The first term is 2-x.
problems.note: The original Word formula confirms that the exponent 2 on the first term is outside the square root.

problems.title: Cosine of an angle between two lines
problems.question: A=(1,5),B=(2,7),C=(3,6). Find the cosine of the acute angle between AB and AC.
problems.idea: Use the two direction vectors.
formulas: cosθ=|u·v|/(|u||v|) for the acute angle between lines.
steps: Their dot product is 1·2+2·1=4. Each length is √5.

problems.title: Use index differences twice
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, a₄₃-a₁₇=52. Find a₁₉-a₇.
problems.idea: Both differences are multiples of the common difference.

problems.title: Fourth parallelogram vertex
problems.question: A=(1,5),B=(2,7),C=(3,3),D are consecutive parallelogram vertices. Find the absolute difference of D’s coordinates.
problems.idea: The diagonals have the same midpoint.

problems.title: Area shared by three equal disks
problems.question: Three circles of radius 3 each pass through the other two centres. Find the area common to all three disks.
problems.idea: The centres form an equilateral triangle; the common region is made of three 60° sectors minus two such triangles.
steps: The centre triangle has side 3. Each bounding arc subtends 60° at the opposite centre.
The sum of the three sectors is 3·(60/360)·9π=9π/2.
Their overlap accounting subtracts two equilateral triangles: 2·9√3/4=9√3/2.

problems.title: Smallest first term of an integer progression
problems.question: An increasing arithmetic progression consists of positive integers and has a₁₇=70. Find the least possible first term.
problems.idea: The common difference is a positive integer.
steps: The largest allowed positive integer d is 4, since d=5 would make a₁ negative.

problems.title: Area from an equal side and its median
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has equal sides 8 cm and median 6 cm to an equal side. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the median formula to find the base.
steps: Thus b²=40 and the half-base is √10.

problems.title: Recover a term from two partial sums
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has Sₙ=1.5n²-3.5n. Find a₃.
problems.idea: The nth term is the difference of consecutive partial sums.

problems.title: Area ratio after a hypotenuse altitude
problems.question: A right triangle has leg ratio 3:2. Its altitude to the hypotenuse divides it into two triangles. Find their area ratio.
problems.idea: The small triangles share the altitude as a common height to the hypotenuse.
formulas: Area ratio=base ratio; hypotenuse projections have ratio of squared legs.
steps: The two projection lengths have ratio 3²:2²=9:4.
The two triangles have the same height to those base segments, so their areas have that ratio.
problems.answer: 9:4, or 4:9 if the triangles are listed in reverse order.

problems.title: Collinear vectors have zero determinant
problems.question: For which k are (-3,k) and (k,-1) collinear?
problems.idea: Set the two-dimensional determinant to zero.
steps: Setting it to zero gives k²=3.

problems.title: First term from two arithmetic-series sums
problems.question: In an arithmetic progression, S₄₈=36 and S₄₉=0. Find a₁.
problems.idea: Use the arithmetic-series formula at both indices.
steps: Subtract the second relation from the first: d=-3/2.

problems.title: Count integers between roots of different indices
problems.question: How many positive integers lie strictly between ∛13 and ⁵√1000?
problems.idea: Compare the endpoints with 2,3,4 using powers.
steps: The lower endpoint lies between 2 and 3, so the smallest eligible integer is 3.
The upper endpoint lies between 3 and 4, so the greatest eligible integer is also 3.

problems.title: Domain of an absolute-value radicand
problems.question: Find the real domain of $\sqrt{4-|x-5|}$.
problems.idea: Require the expression under the root to be nonnegative.

problems.title: Curved gap between two touching circles and a tangent
problems.question: Two externally touching circles have radii r and 3r. Their external common tangent segment AB has length 6. Find the shaded gap bounded by AB and the two arcs to their contact point K.
problems.idea: Find the radii and subtract two circular segments from triangle ABK.
formulas: L²=4Rr for the external tangent of externally touching circles.
Circular segment area=R²(θ-sinθ)/2, with θ in radians; triangle area=base·height/2.
steps: 36=12r² gives r=√3 and R=3√3. Place A=(0,0),B=(6,0), with centres (0,3√3),(6,√3).
The contact point divides the centre segment in ratio 3:1, giving K=(4.5,1.5√3). Triangle ABK has area 9√3/2.
The large arc AK has central angle 60°, so its segment area is 9π/2-27√3/4. The small arc KB has central angle 120°, giving segment area π-3√3/4.
problems.note: The printed coefficients of π in the answer choices give negative areas and do not match the geometry. The solution follows the shaded region shown in the diagram.
